parsed.why: Criminalisation is actively used for police extortion and assault, with forced anal exams documented as torture. Prison placement defaults to birth sex with no statutory route, and care access is poor. Recognition certificates are resident-facing and do not offset these exposures.

Custody follows family-register sex and a trans detainee was held among men with mistreatment documented. Gender-segregated bathhouses lack any stated rule. Courts have ruled for trans people, but no statute covers discrimination, and foreign gender changes have been refused by local offices.

Recognition is available in most states, the capital and national courts set a self-declaration floor, and transfemicide law exists. Violence is high but counts lack denominators, police extortion of trans people is documented, and enforcement of protections is uneven.

Criminalising sections remain in force but are reported unenforced, with no trans-specific violence or custody data. Documented discrimination has no complaint route, and fear of prosecution inhibits reporting. The thin record leans toward the structural risk.

Sodomy law is enforced in a way that deters reporting, with arrests of LGBTQ people after attacks. An active anti-LGBTQ bill is pending, the head of state defended the laws, and public concealment is the norm. A labour-law entitlement is resident-facing only.
